_comment: Copy to labels.json and fill in. Written BEFORE the tool was run - that is the whole point of this file. All five episodes are scaffolded so you only fill blanks; delete nothing. Protocol: eval/README.md.
_how_rejected_works: `rejected` is the fourth measure and the one that teaches you something. `what` and `why_not` are for you; `segments` is what compare.py actually reads, so a rejected span with no block indices is invisible to the report. Record it even roughly - the hit threshold is 50% overlap, not exactness.

labels._episode_note: 138s - series opener, the only episode with no prior context at all
labels.hook: the line or beat that lands in the first 3 seconds
labels.cliffhanger: the unresolved thing it cuts on
labels.why: one line - why a stranger would watch the episode after this

labels._episode_note: 70s - shortest in the season, a 60s promo is 86% of it
201s - longest, most room to choose badly

_how_to_fill_a_span: Write start_block and end_block ONLY - the block your promo opens on and the block it cuts on. Leave start_s, end_s and duration_s as null: `PYTHONPATH=src python -m promo.labels --write` resolves them through the same block table that turns the model's answers into timestamps. You do no arithmetic. Print the worksheet with `PYTHONPATH=src python -m promo.parse <episode>`.
_check_before_running_the_tool: PYTHONPATH=src python -m promo.labels --write   # resolves seconds, names every problem, exits non-zero while anything would break the report
